correctness.rationale: For nonempty finite simple graphs in pure adjacency with equality and no counting, simultaneous peeling of all residual isolated or universal vertices yields an alternating signed sequence with sizes capped at 2 and an optional core C. Every shell is FO²-definable through capture-avoiding reuse of x,y, including a ≥2 test; hence unequal words are distinguished. For equal words Duplicator can preserve shell index, equality and adjacency in an arbitrarily long 2-pebble game; a nonextremal terminal core supplies both a neighbor and a distinct nonneighbor of each pebbled core vertex. The smallest such core is P4, and the recursive shell enumerator gives R(z)=z+[2z²+z⁴(1+z+z²)]/(1-z-z²). I independently calculated 2-pebble stable-refinement classes on all 52 nonempty graph-atlas graphs of orders 1..5 (1,585 pebble states, 18 equivalence classes, stable after four rounds), with exact signature correspondence and minimum-size spectrum (1,2,2,5,8). This is corroboration, not an infinite proof. Scope excludes C², FO³, graph colors and empty graphs.
